URL: https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/5/14/iran-war-why-the-brics-foreign-ministers-meeting-in-india-matters

A meeting of BRICS foreign ministers kicked off in the Indian capital New Delhi on Thursday, with the Iran war likely to cast a shadow on the two-day event.

Attendees:
- Russia: Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov
- South Africa: Ronald Lamola
- Brazil: Mauro Vieira
- Iran: Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi
- Indonesia: Foreign Minister Sugiono
- India: Foreign Minister Subrahmanyam Jaishankar
- China: Ambassador to India Xu Feihong representing (Wang Yi absent due to Trump's Beijing visit)

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi called on fellow BRICS member states to condemn the US and Israel over what he called their "unlawful aggression" against Iran.

India's Foreign Minister Subrahmanyam Jaishankar called for "safe, unimpeded maritime flows" through international waters, as the Strait of Hormuz, through which a fifth of global oil and gas passes, remains under blockade.

The Strait blockade has disrupted 20% of global oil/LNG supplies since early March. Internal BRICS divisions persist, particularly between Iran and UAE over the conflict.
